title: Man. Post. Cap. II §XIV: Placeus — first sin = actuale + habituale; controversy on immediate
pass_a_gloss: But, I say, this does not suffice. It is necessary to advance further. For the sin of Adam first among all embraces two things, actual sin, and habitual sin: that the first of all actual sins, this the first of all habitual: that passed, this remained, and was propagated into posterity, and that it is imputed to us proximately or immediately, since it is within us, no one who is not a Pelagian doubts. Concerning that other, whether it is imputed immediately, the whole controversy stirred among us exists. This distinction, because when the hearer heard the first sin of Adam named it did not at once come into mind, and it had much moment for deciding the question, had to be set before the eyes of the Reader.
pass_b_english: But that, I say, is not enough. We must go further. Adam's first sin among all embraces two things: actual sin and habitual sin—the first of all actual sins, and the first of all habitual ones. The former passed; the latter remained and was propagated to posterity; and that it is imputed to us proximately or immediately, since it is within us, no non-Pelagian doubts. About the other—whether it is imputed immediately—the whole controversy among us has been raised. Because that distinction did not leap to mind as soon as a hearer heard "Adam's first sin" named, and because it mattered much for deciding the question, it had to be set before the reader's eyes.
source_text: At, inquam, hoc non sufficit. Progredi longius oportet. Peccatum enim Adami inter omnia primum duo complectitur, peccatum actuale, & peccatum habituale: illud omnium peccatorum actualium, hoc omnium habitualium primum: illud transiit, hoc mansit, & in posteros propagatum est, & quin nobis proxime seu immediate, cum intra nos sit, imputetur, nemo non Pelagianus ambigit. De altero illo an imputetur immediate, omnis est inter nos excitata controversia. Haec distinctio, quia audienti nominari primum Adae peccatum non statim veniebat in mentem, multumque habebat ad decidendam quaestionem momenti, constituenda fuit ob oculos Lectoris.
